headline: KOSPI's first close below 5,000 since February outweighs foreign futures selling and an IMF growth upgrade: the KTB 3Y falls 1.8bp to 3.725% and the 10Y 1.5bp to 3.966%, almost exactly what a 3bp US Treasury rally implied, while the 20–50Y end slightly higher
summary: KTBs opened firmer with Treasuries, sold off into midday on foreign 10Y futures selling and an IMF call for more BOK tightening, then rallied when KOSPI broke 5,000: the 3Y closed 1.8bp lower at 3.725% (55th percentile of its 1-year range), the 10Y 1.5bp lower at 3.966% (51st) and the 30Y 0.5bp higher at 4.055%. The 2Y–3Y led, so 10s30s steepened 2.0bp to 8.9bp and the 10s20s30s fly rose 2.2bp to 14.5bp (81st), while the 1Y stayed at 3.633% (90th) with the November 26 hike priced. Bills held at 1-year highs (MSB 91-day 3.207%, CD 3.38%, CP 3.84%; CP–CD 46bp, 91st). Spread products roughly kept pace: the KDB 3Y fit is 12.3bp over KTB on the revised fit (16th percentile, rich), AAA bank 1Y 38.1bp (82nd), AA- 3Y 67.7bp (70th) and KEPCO 3Y 41.0bp (81st).
drivers: KOSPI breaks 5,000 and turns the afternoon

KOSPI fell 2.59% to 4,968.48, its first close under 5,000 since Feb 2, as foreigners sold about KRW 1.44tn of stock ahead of Nvidia's results; SK Hynix closed below KRW 1.1m for the first time in seven months. The 3Y had been 1.4bp higher at 11am (3.757%), so the swing into the close was about 3bp and was concentrated in the 2–5Y.
US Treasuries explain the 10Y, not the front end

The US 10Y slipped 3bp to 5.12% on Nov 16 as stocks fell and Fed Chair Warsh warned AI might disappoint. At the 1-year beta of 0.47 that implied −1.4bp for the KTB 10Y against an actual −1.5bp, so Treasuries explain essentially the whole 10Y move; the 3Y's extra fall was local. The KTB–UST 10Y gap is −115bp, still the widest of the past year (0th percentile).
IMF upgrade and foreign futures selling push the other way

The IMF lifted Korea's 2026 growth forecast to 3.9% from 3.3% (2027 to 3.3% from 2.8%), kept inflation at 2.7% and said further monetary tightening is appropriate; Citi also reaffirmed a unanimous hike on Nov 26 and a 3.5% terminal rate. Foreigners sold 3,140 10Y futures and were flat in the 3Y (+6), after buying about 9,000 on Monday.

The 3Y future settled at 103.54 (+6 ticks) against our basket fair value of 103.64, so it is about 10 ticks cheap to cash, little changed from 11 on Monday; the 10Y settled at 108.49 (+14 ticks) against a fair 108.47, about 2 ticks rich. USD/KRW rose 2.5 won to 1,338.2.
data: Solid; supply worries after the fines eased.
view: Today's 10Y move was almost all Treasuries (−1.4bp implied, −1.5bp actual), while the 3Y's extra fall was the local equity bid; over four weeks the KTB 10Y's −13.1bp splits into +10.0bp from Treasuries (weekly beta 0.63, US 10Y +16bp) and −23.1bp of Korea's own rally.

The local drivers still favour bonds: KOSPI is 10.5% lower over four weeks and below 5,000, margin credit is down 12.9% and the rotation signal reads bond rally (weekly +1.13, daily +1.36), though it is off its +1.62 reading of four weeks ago.

Against that, a November 26 hike is priced and the IMF now argues for more, so the front end stays pinned (1Y at the 90th percentile) and I expect the 10Y in a 3.90–4.05% range into the BOK, with the curve flat (3s10s 24.1bp, 3rd percentile).
I keep the 10Y long (average 3.975%, now +0.9bp) and the 30Y-into-50Y switch, which is 0.4bp from target, and stay flat 3s10s until KOSPI recovers 5,300 or the BOK has hiked.

Hedged remains the better way to hold the rotation view: against 0.5 × US 10Y the long is about +5bp, and the signal's hedged record (rally calls right 68%, sell-off calls 69%, Sharpe 1.34, worst drawdown −26bp) beats outright (52%, 57%, 0.91, −36bp); Nvidia results, FOMC minutes (Nov 18) and the BOK's new forecasts (Nov 26) are the main risks.

buckets.name: KTB 1–2Y front end
buckets.why: The 2Y fell 1.4bp to 3.727%, 80th percentile of its 1-year range (average 3.39%), and the 1Y was flat at 3.633% (90th). 2s3s is −0.2bp (1st percentile, average 13bp) and 1s2s 9.4bp (3rd). MSB 91-day (3.207%), CD (3.38%) and CP (3.84%) all sit at 1-year highs and price a hike to 3.25% on Nov 26; Citi sees a 3.5% peak by February.
buckets.call: Keep: buy the 2Y above 3.80%, target 3.65%, stop 3.90%. Not triggered (7bp away).

buckets.name: 3s10s curve
buckets.why: 3s10s steepened 0.3bp to 24.1bp (3rd percentile, average 40bp, 1-year low 20.8bp). The 3s5s10s fly rose 2.3bp to −4.1bp (11th percentile, average 4.3bp) as the 5Y lagged, so the belly is cheapening from very rich levels. Our earlier steepener was stopped on Nov 5.
buckets.call: Stay flat: KOSPI closed at 4,968, so the re-entry trigger was not met. Re-enter the steepener (3 × 3Y vs 1 × 10Y futures, DV01 about KRW 86k each side) only on a KOSPI close above 5,300 or after a BOK hike; target 32bp, stop 19bp.

buckets.name: KTB 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y at 3.966% is at the 51st percentile of a 3.25–4.60% range (average 3.92%). Treasuries implied −1.4bp and the 10Y fell 1.5bp, so the hedged position was unchanged on the day. The new 10Y (26-13), sold in Monday's pre-sale, traded about 5bp rich to the curve.
buckets.call: Long, average 3.975%, stop 4.10%, target 3.85%; hold against about 0.5 × US 10Y. Open, +0.9bp outright, about +5bp hedged.

buckets.name: Ultra-long 30–50Y
buckets.why: 30s50s is −2.6bp (86th percentile, average −9.0bp) after the 50Y rose only 0.2bp against 0.5bp for the 30Y, so the switch from +2.5bp is 5.1bp in favour and 0.4bp from target. The 10s20s30s fly rose 2.2bp to 14.5bp (81st) as the 20Y sold off with the long end.
buckets.call: Keep the 30Y into 50Y switch from +2.5bp; target −3bp, stop +0.5bp. Open, +5.1bp.

buckets.name: KDB 1–3Y vs KTB
buckets.why: On the revised fit (23 trades) the KDB 3Y is 12.3bp over KTB, 16th percentile (average 19.5bp), 0.7bp tighter on the day and 13.9bp tighter this month. The 1Y fit is 28.5bp over (62nd) and KOFIA's 1Y KDB quote 24.2bp (46th). We took profit at 20bp on Nov 13; IBK 3Y is 20.3bp over (50th), and KEXIM's fit uses only 6 trades with a flat slope (low confidence).
buckets.call: Stay flat. Prefer IBK over KDB at 3Y; re-enter KDB overweight only above 20bp.

buckets.name: AAA bank debentures and money market
buckets.why: AAA bank paper (41-trade fit) is 38.1bp over the 1Y KTB, 82nd percentile (average 31bp), unchanged on the day; the 3Y is 30.2bp over (56th). CD and CP were flat at 3.38% and 3.84%, so CP–CD is 46bp (91st, average 29bp) and CD–MSB91 17bp (29th). IBK 1Y is 28.6bp over (56th).
buckets.call: No change: revisit bank paper once CP–CD falls below 35bp; prefer the 1Y over the 3Y if adding.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AA- 3Y)
buckets.why: AA- 3Y fell 1.4bp to 4.402%, less than the KTB 3Y, so the spread widened 0.4bp to 67.7bp (70th percentile, average 62bp). KEPCO 3Y is 41.0bp over (81st, average 35bp) and BBB- minus AA- 583bp (75th). Credit is drifting wider with equities but slowly.
buckets.call: Add AA- only above 75bp or once KOSPI regains 5,300; no trigger hit.

watch: Next: US retail sales and Nvidia results (Nov 17–18 US time), KDI outlook and FOMC minutes (Nov 18), the college entrance exam on Nov 19 (KRX opens an hour late), Nov 1–20 exports around Nov 23, the BOK decision and new forecasts on Nov 26 (hike to 3.25% priced) and the FOMC on Dec 8–9; KTBs take about 0.45–0.5bp per Treasury bp on the day.
